extraction.name: CommonCatalog
extraction.description: CommonCatalog is a dataset of roughly 70 million Creative-Commons-licensed (CC) images sourced from YFCC100M, paired with high-quality synthetic captions generated using a pre-trained BLIP-2 model. It is divided into a commercial subset (CommonCatalog-C, ~26 million images) and a non-commercial subset (CommonCatalog-NC, ~67 million images), and is intended for training text-to-image generative models.
extraction.creator: Aaron Gokaslan (Cornell Tech); A. Feder Cooper (Cornell Tech); Jasmine Collins (Databricks Mosaic); Landan Seguin (Databricks Mosaic); Austin Jacobson (Databricks Mosaic); Mihir Patel (Databricks Mosaic); Jonathan Frankle (Databricks Mosaic); Cory Stephenson (Databricks Mosaic); Volodymyr Kuleshov (Cornell Tech)
extraction.citeAs: Aaron Gokaslan, A. Feder Cooper, Jasmine Collins, Landan Seguin, Austin Jacobson, Mihir Patel, Jonathan Frankle, Cory Stephenson, Volodymyr Kuleshov. CommonCanvas: An Open Diffusion Model Trained with Creative-Commons Images. arXiv:2310.16825v1 [cs.CV], 25 Oct 2023.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The authors started with the YFCC100M dataset, which contains 100 million CC-licensed images and multimedia files with Flickr IDs. They re-scraped these images from Flickr at very high resolution (exceeding 4K) based on the IDs provided in the YFCC100M metadata. Images were filtered by CC license type, excluding non-derivative (ND) licenses, resulting in two datasets: CommonCatalog-C (commercial-use images, ~26 million) and CommonCatalog-NC (commercial + non-commercial images, ~67 million). Synthetic captions were then generated for all collected images using a pre-trained BLIP-2 OPT2.5B model.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Almost all CC images lack the captions necessary to train a text-to-image generative model; only about 30-34% of images had any associated alt-text, and those that did often contained only image titles, URLs, or non-descriptive metadata such as camera model names.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: YFCC100M dataset (100 million CC-licensed images and multimedia files with Flickr IDs); images re-scraped from Flickr at native high resolution (exceeding 4K). The YFCC100M metadata provided the Flickr IDs used for scraping.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human raters performed pairwise preference evaluations: shown a prompt (randomly selected from PartiPrompts) along with two generated images in randomized order (one from SD2-base, one from a CommonCanvas model), and asked which image they preferred. Preference rate reported as fraction of times users selected the CommonCanvas model's image.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: User preference rate computed as the fraction of times human raters selected the CommonCanvas-generated image over the SD2-base-generated image; statistical significance assessed (no statistically significant difference found for CommonCanvas-LNC vs. SD2-base).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: BLIP-2 OPT2.5B (pre-trained image captioning model used to generate synthetic captions for CC images)
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Synthetic captions generated by BLIP-2 exhibit reduced diversity of n-grams compared to ground-truth captions; YFCC100M data is about a decade old and its CC images are not as current as those in LAION-2B; CLIP-FID metric likely favors SD2 as CLIP is trained on a similar style of text as LAION
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: CommonCanvas models underperformed in several categories including faces, general photography, and paintings; CC images are relatively scarce (~70 million) compared to LAION-2B (~2 billion); almost all CC images lack the captions necessary to train a high-quality T2I model; YFCC100M data is about a decade old and not as current as LAION-2B; synthetic captions have reduced n-gram diversity; although trained on Creative-Commons images, adversarial prompts can still produce content resembling iconic characters
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and models are intended to address copyright concerns associated with web-scraped training data; training on CC-licensed images with known provenance avoids unclear copyright status of LAION datasets, which are subject to ongoing copyright lawsuits; the CommonCanvas models are qualitatively less likely to generate recognizable copyrighted characters (e.g., Disney characters, Snoopy) compared to SD2
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training text-to-image generative diffusion models; evaluating data- and compute-efficient training recipes for T2I models; serving as an open, provenanced alternative to web-scraped datasets like LAION for training generative models; fine-tuning for specific image categories by supplementing with additional datasets
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to augment CommonCatalog with Creative-Commons images from other sources in future work; the CommonCatalog dataset and CommonCanvas models are released on HuggingFace and GitHub
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: Missing captions for CC images were filled using a pre-trained BLIP-2 OPT2.5B model to generate synthetic captions. Approximately 31% of images had existing alt-text; the remainder had captions synthesized via BLIP-2. This 'telephoning' approach used lossy compression from image to text to produce descriptive captions where none existed.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was split into commercial (CommonCatalog-C, ~26M images) and non-commercial (CommonCatalog-NC, ~67M images) subsets based on license type. Images with non-derivative (ND) licenses were excluded. For captioning, all images were center-cropped and resized to a maximum of 512x512 pixels prior to BLIP-2 caption generation, though native resolution was retained for diffusion model training. Random subsets of LAION-2B (ranging from 1M to 1.1B examples) were used to investigate data scarcity.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were re-scraped from Flickr at high resolution (exceeding 4K) based on YFCC100M metadata. Images with non-derivative (ND) licenses were excluded. For caption generation, all images were center-cropped and resized to a maximum size of 512x512 pixels before being passed to BLIP-2 for synthetic caption generation. At training time, images remain in their native resolution. VAE and text encoder latents were precomputed over the entire training dataset as a one-time preprocessing step.
